answer.ruling: A player rules a clearing if they have more warriors plus buildings there than every other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.

answer.ruling: Move any positive number of your warriors/pawns from one clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including multiple times in one action.

answer.ruling: Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.

answer.ruling: Choose a clearing containing your warriors or pawn and an enemy defender; you need not rule it. Defender may play a matching ambush (birds wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise it deals two immediate hits, not limited by defender warriors, and is discarded; battle ends immediately if no attacking warriors or pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them), roll (higher die is attacker hits, lower defender hits; ties equal; each side's rolled hits are capped by its warriors, except Alliance defense reverses dice and Vagabond uses undamaged swords), then after-roll effects (attacker orders if both sides have them). Count hits by adding extra hits and subtracting ignored hits; attacker gets one extra defenseless hit if defender has no warriors (for Vagabond, no undamaged swords). Deal hits: each removes one opposing piece; the hit-taking side chooses removal order but removes all its warriors before buildings/tokens, and orders its removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal counted hits even if warriors are removed during this step; the roll cap does not change retroactively. Vagabond takes hits as item damage.

answer.ruling: Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, including a defender and removals outside battle.

answer.ruling: Pay one crafting icon at a time using one workshop, roost, or sympathy (Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance) in a clearing matching that icon's suit; each such piece may activate only once per turn. The crafting piece's clearing determines its suit, not the card's suit. A three-color question-mark accepts any suit. Vagabond pays one face-up undamaged hammer per icon and its current clearing must match every icon; its pawn may activate repeatedly in a turn, but repeated use does not waive hammer costs. If an item card's matching item token is absent from map supply, it cannot be crafted. Only an identical persistent effect in your own play area blocks crafting it again; another player's copy does not.

answer.ruling: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.

When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance into your hand; an available bird dominance remains bird, so the payment must be a bird. Taking it and activating it are separate actions, and neither uses a faction action allowance.

answer.part: Two-player deck, hand, ruins and map items
answer.ruling: For two players remove all four dominance cards, shuffle the shared deck, and each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. Set out the separate item supply of 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Only if Vagabond is present, during its faction setup put one each of the R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword beneath the four ruins, shuffle the stacks with identities hidden, and return one stack to each empty R slot; otherwise ruins have no hidden items.
answer.evidence: Setup — Standard Setup and Hidden ruin items

answer.ruling: Set factions up in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. This order does not determine turn order.

evidence: Setup — Standard Setup and Hidden ruin items

answer.ruling: Only Marquise may place pieces in the Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply, including when removed outside battle. Without a Keep there is no Hospitals destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.

Marquise crafts with workshops first, then takes up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order; Recruit is limited to once per turn. A March is one compound action of up to two moves and cannot be interrupted to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.

Choose a clearing you rule that has an open slot and choose a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings linked to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered space. You need the full wood cost, the building, and a legal open slot; otherwise you cannot build.

In order: Emergency Orders draws one card if your hand is empty; Add to Decree adds one or two hand cards, at most one bird, to any columns (no size limit); A New Roost applies only if no roost is on the map, placing one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.

Craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; within a column choose card order freely. Bird cards are wild in each column. Recruit matches a clearing with a roost and places one warrior at one chosen roost (Charismatic: two). Move matches the origin and moves at least one warrior under normal path and rule requirements. Battle matches the battle clearing and initiates a battle there with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build matches the target and places one roost in a clearing you rule with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil begins immediately; you cannot skip it or continue to another column.

evidence: Eyrie Dynasties — Daylight: resolve the Decree

answer.ruling: Lose one VP for each bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none is face up, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends, but map warriors and buildings remain. Take the normal Evening: score the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five.

Whenever another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player adds one matching hand card (birds count) to Supporters per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If the stack is full, discard the incoming card; the payment or no-match draw still occurs.

answer.part: Revolt and Spread Sympathy timing, eligibility, cost and result
answer.ruling: Both occur during Birdsong; complete all Revolts before any Spread Sympathy, and each can be done any number of times. Once spreading begins, no return to Revolt that Birdsong, so new sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong Revolt. For both, every supporter spent matches the target clearing (birds wild). Revolt targets a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on your board; spend two matching supporters, remove all enemy pieces there and score one VP per enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, place warriors equal to matching-suit sympathetic clearings including this one, and one warrior in Officers. Spread Sympathy targets an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; spend the matching supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter if the clearing has at least three warriors of one other player (Martial Law). Place sympathy and score its uncovered VP; only one sympathy per clearing, and Keep's placement ban applies. If pieces cannot all be placed, place the maximum possible; Vagabond pawn is damaged (three items) rather than removed by Revolt's remove-all effect.

answer.ruling: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with a base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. Each officer permits one Evening military operation, and operations do not consume officers. Organize is an Evening operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there and score its uncovered VP; it spends no supporters and has no adjacency or Martial Law cost, but legal token placement is required. When a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing including birds, remove half officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters down to five.

answer.ruling: Birdsong Refresh first counts tea already face up on Refresh track, flips two exhausted items per such tea, then flips three more; tea refreshed now gives no extra refresh now. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, ignoring effects that prevent movement out. Normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination contains any hostile-faction warriors; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, return all damaged items to Satchel face up and move ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; this Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Always draw one card plus one per face-up coin on track even after Rest.

Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or track, scores one VP if an item is taken, and removes the ruin/freeing its building slot when its last item is taken. Quest requires a face-up quest matching the clearing; exhaust its two listed items, put it in completed quests, then choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards; draw a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.

Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile (with a special timing rule for allied warriors taken as hits). On your own turn in battle, Infamy scores one extra VP for each hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; hostile building/token removal in that battle is thus one normal VP plus one Infamy VP. No Infamy on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though it may still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that faction has no warriors there may you instead remove another of its faction pieces. Strike is not battle.

With four or more players, during Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to coalition with another player not already in coalition, whose VP is lowest among all players other than Vagabond (choose among ties). Place Vagabond's score marker on that player's faction board and stop scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond also wins, including through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies; coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers. If the partner is Hostile, its marker resets to Indifferent.

Cards override Law, Law overrides Learning to Play; follow general and faction rules together when possible, with faction rule prevailing if incompatible. “Cannot” is absolute unless explicitly overridden; an ordinary card does not override it absent explicit override.

answer.part: Unclear simultaneous effects and March interruption
answer.ruling: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action, so it cannot be interrupted between moves to spend a bird card or take another action.

answer.part: Phase timings and last turn step
answer.ruling: At-start effects happen before all other effects of that phase; at-end effects follow all other effects in that phase, before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except explicitly end-of-Evening/turn actions.

Hand size is public, contents private; reveal/show a hand only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected; the deck cannot. Deals are non-binding; cards may transfer only as instructed, and actions require no consent.

answer.ruling: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple payments. When instructed to give/discard non-bird-suit cards, birds must be treated as that suit; birds cannot substitute when the instruction explicitly requires a bird.

Pieces are finite and proxies are not allowed. If an instruction cannot place all prompted pieces, place the maximum possible and do not voluntarily place fewer. Shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and it does not waive the Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions; an uncompleted Decree action causes Turmoil.

answer.ruling: Placed pieces normally come from supply, or the leftmost track space; removed faction pieces normally return to supply, and tracked pieces return to the rightmost empty track space. Removed items are removed permanently. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.

answer.ruling: Resolve a forced action as if the affected player chose it; that player's own abilities and restrictions still apply. A player forced to battle makes that battle's decisions.

An enemy cannot place a piece in the Keep clearing; replacement requires both removal and placement to be possible, so replacement cannot bypass that ban. A swap ignores move/place restrictions; ordinary move and place remain distinct procedures.

answer.ruling: If multiple players reach 30 VP simultaneously, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins, including the current player.

A forest is adjacent to clearings touching it without crossing a printed path, and to forests separated by just one printed path. Winter's river also divides forests as paths do; rivers otherwise are not paths. Fall has no special rules. Vagabond Slip uses this forest adjacency.

answer.ruling: Supply 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner starting clearing. Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.

Supply 20 warriors. Put one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep the others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into that leader's listed columns. Put the other six roosts on the track from right to left.

Supply 10 warriors; put three bases in their matching board spaces and ten sympathy on its track. Draw three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from the three-card hand. Alliance starts with no map pieces or officers.

Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's S-marked items: tea, coins and bags go face up on matching tracks; other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. Set each other faction's relationship marker to Indifferent. (R-marked ruin items are handled separately.)

Recommended total Reach is at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, Alliance 3. The Law also permits adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.

In Birdsong place one wood per sawmill in its clearing, limited by the finite supply of eight wood (one per sawmill, including multiple in one clearing). Overwork during Daylight spends a card matching a sawmill clearing to place one wood there; it uses the same eight-wood supply. In Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.

No: Supporters can be spent only for suit, not used to craft. Alliance can inspect its separate face-down Supporters stack. Supporters do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit.

No. All Revolts must be completed before starting Spread Sympathy. Once spreading starts, Alliance cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong, so newly spread sympathy cannot be used for a same-Birdsong Revolt.

No. Martial Law adds one matching supporter only if the target clearing has at least three warriors of one other player; two enemy players with two each do not meet that condition. Martial Law applies to Spread Sympathy, not Organize; Organize has no Martial Law cost.

answer.ruling: Take up to the number of officers in operations, in any order and repetition: Move (one normal move), Battle (initiate one battle), Recruit (place one warrior at one clearing with a base), or Organize (remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, score uncovered VP). Officers remain and are not consumed. After operations, draw one plus uncovered draw bonuses, then discard to five.
The pawn cannot be removed. An enemy effect that removes all enemy pieces from its clearing instead damages three Vagabond items.

Vagabond's rolled hits are capped by its undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or down; exhausted swords count, damaged swords do not. As defender it is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Hits against Vagabond damage one undamaged item each; if none remain, excess hits are ignored.

answer.ruling: Face-up tea/coins/bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty matching track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting a track item sends it to Satchel. Damaged items cannot pay actions even if face up; action exhaustion requires a face-up, undamaged item.

Satchel plus Damaged box capacity is six items plus two for each face-up bag on its track. Items on tracks do not count toward load. Check capacity at the end of Evening, after draw/discard; do not check immediately on acquiring an item. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit.

Forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if able. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Refresh flips exhausted items face up according to tea already on the Refresh track plus three; Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face.

answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged item of any type and give a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. Vagabond may then take one item from that player's Crafted Items box face up into Satchel/track, but an item is not required to perform Aid. To improve a non-Hostile relationship, Aid that faction the printed number of times in the same turn; each Aid counts toward only one improvement. Advance and score the new space's VP. Hostile markers cannot improve through Aid.

At Allied, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may force warriors of one Allied faction to accompany its move to the destination, subject to those warriors' own movement restrictions (including rule and Eyrie tie advantage); not on moves specified to be alone. At the start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may treat one Allied faction's warriors in the battle clearing as its own to increase its rolled-hit limit by their number plus all undamaged swords. They may join against another enemy, but cannot be used to attack their own faction.

In battle using Allied warriors as your own, if Vagabond removes more allied warriors than the number of items it damages in that battle, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it. This overrides ordinary hostility timing for those allied warriors removed as hits against another enemy.
